title: LibreChat MCP OAuth -- T1528 unvalidated resource-metadata redirects a token to a malicious server
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-54030 (GHSA-gvpj-vm2f-2m23,
CVSS 8.0 HIGH), a self-reported advisory for LibreChat, an
enhanced ChatGPT-clone supporting multiple AI providers.

Prior to 0.8.5, LibreChat's MCP OAuth implementation
(`packages/api/src/mcp/oauth/handler.ts:542-548`) fetched OAuth
Protected Resource metadata (RFC 9728) from the configured MCP server
and used its `resource` field to build the authorization URL --
WITHOUT verifying that field matches the server the operator actually
configured. RFC 9728 section 7.3 requires exactly this check
(the metadata's `resource` value must match the URL it was requested
from) and section 3.3 says data must be discarded on mismatch; LibreChat
implemented neither. A malicious MCP server hosted at
`fake-mcp.com/mcp` can therefore publish resource metadata claiming
`resource: real-mcp.com/mcp`, causing a victim who configured LibreChat
to point at the attacker's server to complete an OAuth consent flow that
LOOKS like it authorizes the legitimate server, while the resulting
access token is delivered to the attacker's server instead.

Detection logic flags the structural mismatch the fix specifically
validates against: an OAuth authorization request whose `resource`
parameter's origin differs from the MCP server origin the client
actually connected to, to fetch the metadata.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (danny-avila, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 0.8.5 (compares the metadata's resource origin
against the configured server's origin and rejects a mismatch).
